title: fix(core)!: a context placeholder on a date, datetime or time field is refused, as the id it resolves to already was
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-bill"} -->
_Requested by **Bill** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wg?thread=cmsg_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wgEpYDjddvdg2ymktFMmNiYa)_

Fixes #35394

Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — `skills/objectstack-query/rules/filters.md` ("Session tokens") teaches `{current_user_id}` / `{current_org_id}` as the signed-in user's and organization's ids, shown on an id column (`owner_id`), and teaches no temporal use; a context placeholder on a date, datetime or time field now takes the refusal the literal id already took, which needs no new rule in the skills

## 维护者速读

- 用户看到的变化：在日期、日期时间、时间字段上用「当前用户」「当前组织」占位符做筛选，现在会直接报错并点名字段；以前不报错，却悄悄返回错误的记录（例如「早于」返回全部、「等于」返回空）。
- 为什么：这种筛选拿用户编号去比日期，本来就不可能对；直接写用户编号早就会被拒绝，占位符绕过了这道检查。
- 如果判断错：只影响这类本就算不对的筛选；「本周一」等日期占位符照常可用，其他占位符的报错不变。
- 需要您做的：无。

### 席位核对

- Read first: `packages/core/src/utils/temporal-comparand.ts` (the new `PLACEHOLDER_AT_THE_TEMPORAL_RULE` table and its `return false` row); the `[#35394]` describe at the end of `packages/objectql/src/engine-temporal-comparand-door.test.ts`; `.changeset/35394-context-token-temporal-door.md`.
- Two-minute check: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/core exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/utils/temporal-comparand.test.ts`, expect 30 passed including two `[#35394]` tests.
- Landing: L1-a, then seat 5's `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review on the narrowing face; the area lands.

## What changes

`isUninterpretableTemporalComparand` (`@objectstack/core`) stepped around every known `{placeholder}` except a period key, so a context placeholder on a `date`, `datetime` or `time` column was never judged by the temporal-comparand door, resolved to the caller's id, and compared as text at the driver. The step-around is now one row per placeholder kind, `PLACEHOLDER_AT_THE_TEMPORAL_RULE`, typed over the spec's `classifyFilterToken` kinds so a kind the spec adds is a compile error until someone decides it:

| kind | at the temporal rule | why |
|---|---|---|
| `date-macro` | stepped around | the door judges it by its year once resolved (`judgeResolvedToken`, unchanged) |
| `unknown` | stepped around | the resolver refuses it by name, `FILTER_TOKEN_UNKNOWN` / 400 |
| `record-context` | stepped around | the resolver refuses it by name, `FILTER_TOKEN_UNRESOLVED` / 400 |
| `period-key` | judged as written | as before (the `{current_iso_week}` precedent) |
| `context` | judged as written | **new**: resolves to an id, which no temporal rule reads |

No change to `packages/objectql/src/temporal-comparand-door.ts`: the door already asks this predicate before resolution on `where` and on `having`, so the refusal reaches `find`, `findOne`, `count`, `aggregate` (both positions), `update` and `delete`, and a context placeholder needs no post-resolution judgement (it never resolves to a temporal value: `CONTEXT_TOKENS` is `current_user_id`, `current_org_id`).

The refusal, measured on InMemoryDriver (the same envelope on SqlDriver):

```text
find('p'): filter on 'due_on' compares a declared date field against "{current_user_id}" at where.due_on.$lt, which is not a date value this platform can interpret. Write a "YYYY-MM-DD" calendar day that exists, or a relative-date placeholder the resolver knows, e.g. "{30_days_ago}" / "{current_month_start}". The filter was NOT applied. ...
```

**Route note.** The card's "Expected" and the dispatch's assumption A1 read "the step-around applies to date-macro placeholders only". Measured, that would also move an unknown placeholder (`{TODAY}`) and `{record_id}` on a temporal column from the resolver's by-name refusal to this door's "not a date value", against existing pins (`engine-aggregate-having-temporal-door.test.ts` "an unknown {placeholder} is not this door's verdict", `engine-aggregate-positions.test.ts` `placed_on $gte {TODAY}`). Those two kinds therefore stay stepped around; the card's done-when (context and period-key placeholders refused, a date macro still resolving) holds in full.

**Other readers of the predicate (measured, not edited).** `import-coerce.ts` asks `classifyFilterToken(s) !== null` first, so no placeholder reaches it. `record-validator.ts`: the `date` / `datetime` arm requires `Date.parse` to read the value, and the `time` arm requires `classifyFilterToken(value) === null`, so no placeholder reaches the predicate there either. `service-analytics` (`comparand-shape.ts`, `NativeSQLStrategy.canHandle`): `resolveQueryTokens` runs before `resolveStrategy`, so the walk only ever sees the resolved id, which it already declined; the analytics suite is green unchanged.

## Where else the answer moves (contract review 7011051316, S1)

Mirrored verbatim from the changeset at `cd3f820f8`; each line was measured before and after on a real engine (os-dev-report 7013135201). `aggregate`'s refusal covers its `where`, each aggregation's `filter` and its `having`.

The refusal comes from the temporal-comparand door, which runs one stage ahead of the placeholder resolver. So a caller with no session, which got `FILTER_TOKEN_UNRESOLVED` (400) for this spelling on a temporal field, now gets `INVALID_FILTER` (400). On an id or text field it still gets `FILTER_TOKEN_UNRESOLVED`.

The engine's judge-only admission runs the same door, and so do two of its readers:

- `IObjectQLEngine.judgeFilter` answers `{ ok: false, code: 'INVALID_FILTER', status: 400 }` for this spelling on a temporal field. With a session it answered `{ ok: true }`; without one it answered `FILTER_TOKEN_UNRESOLVED`.
- Lint's row-scope predicate rule (`rls-predicate-unenforceable`) still refuses a predicate such as `due_on < '{current_user_id}'`. The finding now quotes `INVALID_FILTER / 400` with the hint to rewrite the comparison, where it quoted `FILTER_TOKEN_UNRESOLVED / 400` with the hint to write the caller's value as a `current_user` key.
- Analytics read-scope admission: when the analytics service asks the engine to admit an object's read scope, a scope that compares a `date` or `datetime` field with a context placeholder is now refused at compile, `READ_SCOPE_COMPILE_FAILED` (500, fail-closed). After the upgrade, a dashboard or analytics query over such an object answers 500 until that clause is rewritten as below.

The fix for an author: compare the date field against a date (a `YYYY-MM-DD` day, an ISO-8601 instant, or a date macro such as `{30_days_ago}`), and compare the user or organization id against the field that holds it, such as `owner_id`. In a row-level-security predicate, write `owner == current_user.id`.

## Tests

- `packages/core/src/utils/temporal-comparand.test.ts`: `[#35394]` — every `CONTEXT_TOKENS` entry, both spellings (`{x}`, `${x}`), on `date` / `datetime` / `time`, answers `true`, as the literal id does; the discriminating half keeps date macros, every `RECORD_CONTEXT_TOKENS` entry and three unknown spellings at `false`.
- `packages/objectql/src/engine-temporal-comparand-door.test.ts`: `[#35394]` — `{current_user_id}`, `${current_user_id}`, `{current_org_id}` on the three kinds, under `$eq` / `$lt` / `$gte` / `$gt`, implicit equality, `$in`, `count` and a predicate `delete`: `INVALID_FILTER` / 400 naming the field, zero driver reads; the literal id takes the same refusal; `{current_user}` stays `FILTER_TOKEN_UNKNOWN` and `{record_id}` stays `FILTER_TOKEN_UNRESOLVED`. Positive controls in the same test: the token still resolves to `usr_1` on a text column, and `{current_week_start}` still resolves to `2026-11-16` on a `date` column.
- `packages/objectql/src/engine-aggregate-having-temporal-door.test.ts`: `[#35394]` — both context tokens on `max(placed_on)` in `having`, native and row paths: `INVALID_FILTER` / 400 naming `having.last_placed.$lt`, zero reads.

The objectql pins use this file's recording driver, whose `reads` assert the refusal precedes every driver; the real-driver reading is the probe below.

## Acceptance notes

- The refusal's consequence sentence is the junk-literal class's ("compare false for EVERY row"), the same words the literal id and the `{current_iso_week}` placeholder already get. Measured, `$lt` answered every row rather than none; the sentence is pre-existing, shared by the whole class, and not changed here.
- `temporal-comparand-door.ts`'s module note still says "`{placeholder}` strings are stepped around" in its Scope section, true before the period-key change and stale since; it is outside this card's file surface and not edited.
- Real-driver pins at the REST door (`packages/rest/src/data-temporal-write-real-day-iso.test.ts` carries the `{current_iso_week}` ones over SqlDriver) are outside the claimed file surface; the real-driver evidence is the before / after probe below.
